## MoodBuro 0.3.4

This release brings the timetable changes of InspCal 2.3 to MoodBuro.

### One group choice for repeated sessions

- When several sessions of the same course offer the same groups in a week, the session panel now offers to apply your group to the others, for example “Apply “Groupe 2” to the 2 Other Sessions”.
- Opening a session you have not answered yet offers the group you already chose for the matching sessions, when it is the only one.
- Answers you already gave are never changed. Sessions whose participation is optional, other half-promotions and Friday rotation workshops (which already share one choice) are left out.

### Timetable reading

- The vendored InspCal engine is updated to InspCal 2.3 (`0a7c371`). In weeks read or edited from now on, outdated links to the former ENA Moodle's resource pages are no longer listed under speakers; direct biography files are kept.
- Weeks already saved keep their links until you edit their choices. Saving such a week again may list those sessions as changed once, because their outdated link is removed.
- Engine version, institution rules and the adapter contract are unchanged, and the public fixtures still match InspCal's reviewed goldens.

### Saved course files

- A saved copy of a course file that looks like a timetable PDF now offers **Open as Timetable** in Courses › course files, like Downloads already did. It reads the copy saved on this Mac and opens the week in Agenda › Timetable.

### Maintenance

- Tauri 2.12.7 and its macOS webview and window components, with other compatible Rust and JavaScript dependency updates.
- French: the group-choice button keeps the group name and its guillemets together on one line.

### Install or upgrade

From MoodBuro 0.2.0 or later, check for updates in Settings → General. For a first installation or an earlier version, download the universal macOS DMG (Apple Silicon and Intel), verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, quit MoodBuro, then drag the app into Applications.

The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. macOS may require first-launch approval in System Settings → Privacy & Security. macOS 12 is the configured minimum; full supported-platform, Intel runtime and installed update qualification remain in progress.

### Assets

- Universal `.dmg` installer
- Signed `.app.tar.gz` update archive and `.sig`
- `latest.json` stable update manifest for both Mac architectures
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`
